name: Standard Weak-Tackle Flex vs Power Sweep
formation: 21P Offset-I Right Power Sweep Left vs Flex

summary.motive: Use the one-yard flex alignment to occupy blockers passively while three defenders converge independently on the sweep point of attack without needing a blocked lane.
summary.keyDefender: The flexed weak-side tackle on his free lateral chase
summary.whyItWorks: Sweep blocking schemes assign the playside guard to reach a defender who starts beyond his reach window, so the flexed tackle runs free down the line as a fourth pursuer.
summary.failureMode: A crack return block by the receiver on the forcing corner removes the third converger and lets the sweep bounce cleanly outside.

beats.title: 1. The Flex Picture
beats.text: The weak tackle lines up a full yard off the ball, denying the guard an immediate target while giving himself an unobstructed runway parallel to the line of scrimmage.

beats.title: 2. Sweep Flow Meets the Free Lane
beats.text: As the sweep launches, the flexed tackle chases laterally down the line untouched because no blocker can reach him in time, while WILL triggers downhill immediately.

beats.title: 3. The Edge Holds
beats.text: The fullback kick-out is absorbed square by the defensive end, who turns the ball carrier back toward the pursuing wave instead of letting him turn the corner.

beats.title: 4. Three-Defender Convergence
beats.text: The flexed tackle chasing from inside, the triggering linebacker from depth, and the forcing corner from the perimeter all arrive simultaneously for a no-gain stop.

relations.tell: The weak-side tackle aligns a visible yard off the line of scrimmage with hands free, unlike his strong-side partner who stays shaded on the snap.
